measures.eligibility_reason: Lina's Bakery Sdn. Bhd. meets all SME criteria: paid-up capital of RM100,000 (well under RM2.5 million), gross business income of RM824,300 (well under RM50 million), and is a registered company. The business qualifies for the tiered SME tax rates of 15% on the first RM150,000 of taxable income and 17% on RM150,001–RM600,000, instead of the flat 24% rate. Based on FY2025 profit before tax of RM93,500, this results in approximately RM8,415 in annual tax savings compared to the flat 24% rate.

measures.estimated_benefit: Approximately RM8,415/year in tax savings. Calculation: At SME tiered rate, tax on RM93,500 (FY2025 PBT) = 15% x RM93,500 = RM14,025. At flat 24% rate = 24% x RM93,500 = RM22,440. Savings = RM8,415/year. Actual savings depend on chargeable income after capital allowances and other deductions.
what_is_needed: File annual tax return under self-assessment with LHDN (handled by accountant LK Tan & Associates).
The SME tiered rates are applied automatically based on paid-up capital and gross income declared in the return — no separate application needed.

measures.eligibility_reason: Lina's Bakery qualifies as an MSME (small enterprise in the services sector: RM824,300 annual sales, 8 employees — well within the SME definition of sales up to RM3 million or up to 29 employees). The business has a quotation for an e-invoicing module (RM2,400 from KedaiDigital, QT-2026-0917) and does not currently have an e-invoicing system in place. The e-invoicing implementation cost can be claimed as a tax deduction of up to RM50,000 per year for ESG-related expenditures, available from YA 2024 through 2027.

measures.estimated_benefit: Up to RM50,000/year in deductible ESG expenses. Based on the known e-invoicing module cost of RM2,400/year (KedaiDigital quotation), the estimated tax savings = RM2,400 x 15% (marginal SME tax rate) = RM360/year. If the business incurs additional ESG-related expenses (e.g., energy-efficient equipment, waste reduction), the maximum potential tax savings is up to RM7,500/year (RM50,000 x 15%).
what_is_needed: Implement the e-invoicing module (quotation already in hand from KedaiDigital, RM2,400 for 12-month subscription).
Keep the invoice/receipt from KedaiDigital as supporting documentation.
Claim the deduction in the annual tax return (YA 2026) — accountant LK Tan & Associates can handle this.
If claiming additional ESG expenses, maintain supporting documentation for all ESG-related expenditures.

measures.measure_name: Stamp duty exemption on employment contracts
measures.eligibility_reason: The business has employees earning RM3,000/month or below: E005 (Nurul Izzah, RM2,000), E006 (Chong Wei Jie, RM1,900), and E007 (Aisyah binti Rosli, RM1,800). However, these existing employment contracts were signed before 1 January 2026, so they do not qualify for the exemption (which requires contracts dated on or after 1 January 2026). The business plans to hire 2 new front counter/online order staff from November 2026 at approximately RM1,900/month each — these new contracts will be dated after 1 January 2026 and will qualify for the stamp duty exemption. The exemption is small in monetary terms (RM10 per contract) but applies automatically.

rule_by_rule_evaluation.rule: Employment contract salary must be RM3,000/month or below
rule_by_rule_evaluation.detail: 3 existing employees earn at or below RM3,000/month: E005 (RM2,000), E006 (RM1,900), E007 (RM1,800). Additionally, 2 planned new hires from November 2026 at ~RM1,900/month each will also qualify.

rule_by_rule_evaluation.rule: Employment contract must be dated on or after 1 January 2026
rule_by_rule_evaluation.detail: The 2 planned new hires (from November 2026) will have contracts dated after 1 January 2026, qualifying for the exemption. The 3 existing employees (E005, E006, E007) have contracts dated before 2026 (joined 2023-2025) and do not qualify for the exemption. However, if any existing unstamped contracts are submitted for stamping after 1 January 2026, the exemption may apply — the owner should consult LHDN or their accountant.

measures.estimated_benefit: Approximately RM20 in stamp duty savings for the 2 planned new hires (RM10 per contract x 2 contracts). If the owner also stamps the 3 existing qualifying employees' contracts now, an additional RM30 could be saved (subject to LHDN confirmation that contracts signed before 2026 can still benefit from the exemption when stamped after the effective date).
what_is_needed: When hiring 2 new staff from November 2026, ensure employment contracts are dated on or after 1 January 2026.
Submit contracts for stamping with LHDN — the exemption applies automatically for salaries at or below RM3,000/month.
Consult LK Tan & Associates or LHDN about whether the 3 existing qualifying employees' contracts (signed before 2026) can still be stamped under the exemption.

measures.eligibility_reason: Lina's Bakery meets most criteria for the GGSM4 financing guarantee: 100% Malaysian-owned (exceeds 51% requirement), SSM-registered under the Companies Act 2016, annual sales of RM824,300 (well under the RM20 million services threshold), and classified as an SME (PMKS). The business could use this guarantee for working capital and capital expenditure (e.g., the planned RM45,000 deck oven purchase). However, GGSM4 is targeted at specific focus sectors: Bumiputera, Halal, Tourism, and High Growth High Value sectors. Food & Beverage is not explicitly listed. The business could qualify if it holds Halal certification (placing it in the 'Halal' focus sector) or if shareholders are Bumiputera (placing it in the 'Bumiputera' focus sector) — but both are currently unknown. If neither applies, the business may still be eligible for other SJPP schemes (SJMK, etc.) with lower maximum amounts (RM10 million) and broader sector coverage, but those are separate schemes from GGSM4.

measures.estimated_benefit: If eligible: government guarantee of up to 80% of financing amount, significantly improving access to bank loans and reducing collateral requirements. For the planned RM45,000 deck oven purchase, the guarantee would cover up to RM36,000 (80%). The business pays a guarantee fee of 0.75% per annum (minimum RM500). Actual monetary benefit = access to financing that might otherwise be unavailable or require more collateral. Not a direct cash grant.

measures.eligibility_reason: Lina's Bakery meets the SME criteria for the proposed Budget 2027 tax rate reduction: paid-up capital of RM100,000 (under RM2.5 million) and gross business income of RM824,300 (under RM50 million). When this measure takes effect (expected YA 2027), the business would benefit from a 1 percentage point reduction on the first RM600,000 of taxable income (15% to 14% on first RM150,000; 17% to 16% on RM150,001-RM600,000). Based on current PBT of RM93,500, this would save approximately RM935/year. Note: this measure was announced in Budget 2027 on 9 October 2026 and is not yet in force — implementation details are pending from LHDN/MOF.

measures.eligibility_reason: This measure raises the minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000/month, effective June 2027, but applies only to employers with annual sales of RM50 million or above. MSMEs with annual sales below RM50 million are explicitly exempted. Lina's Bakery has annual sales of RM824,300 — well below the RM50 million threshold — so the business is exempt from the revised minimum wage rate. This is a favorable outcome: the business is not required to raise wages to RM2,000/month. Note: 2 of the 8 current employees (E006: RM1,900 and E007: RM1,800) earn below RM2,000/month, and the 2 planned new hires are at RM1,900/month — but since the business is exempt, no wage adjustments are required.
